Working with PowerPoint

The workflow itself does not require much adjustment to work with PowerPoint, though clean(pptx_section_offset = TRUE) is often useful to adjust header levels when Section Header slides are used. A number of specific helper functions can also help.

Quarto-produced PowerPoint presentations often require different styling and formatting than other output types. knittogether has a set of functions to make these easier to apply, typically with checks to ensure these styles do not apply to HTML outputs. These functions are simplest to use in Quarto-generated content but can be inserted into content imported from markdown if desired.

Slide templates

A limited number of slide layouts are supported by Pandoc. It is advisable to create a master slide template limited to these layouts, with useful features such as slide numbers and styling applied to elements such as text.

Backgrounds

The function pptx_section_slide() allows for background images to be added to slides. These images need to be provided in the right dimensions.

Columns

The functions pptx_col_start(), pptx_col_break(), and pptx_col_end() allow easy addition of columns.

Starting a new slide

By default, level 1 (#) and level 2 (##) headings create a new slide, with all subsequent content placed on that slide. This can produce content that exceeds slide size and, unlike HTML slide formats, there is currently no practical way to resize text except by globally reducing text size in the master template. It can therefore be useful to add slide breaks throughout the text. This can be done manually with slide_break() and automatically on a string with auto_slide_break(). In Quarto-generated documents, these are straightforward to apply, though some trial and error may be needed to ensure content fits slides. If exact locations are required within Word/markdown documents, breaks can be added manually in markdown (with reproducibility trade-offs), added programmatically (e.g., matching text or at specific line numbers), or with inline code such as `r knittogether::slide_break()` at the relevant location.

Citations

There is no Zotero support for PowerPoint. Therefore it can often be easier to create them in R. If citations are done in PowerPoint they must be done so manually by creating a library in Zotero, adding the references and then copying the Citation Key for each reference into the PowerPoint, prefixing it with [@ and suffixing it with ] so that it aligns with the pandoc syntax outlined in vignette("citations") and matches the bibliography. These references will be read into markdown and subsequent qmd outputs.
